After this lesson, you should be able to add and subtract simple fractions and mixed numbers, whether with regrouping or without regrouping.
Fractions are similar if they have the same bottom number (denominator) and dissimilar if they have different bottom numbers.
Examine each pair of fractions and determine whether they are similar or dissimilar. Choose SIMILAR or DISSIMILAR for each pair.
After this lesson, you should be able to add and subtract simple fractions and mixed numbers, whether with regrouping or without regrouping.
After this lesson, you should be able to solve both routine and non-routine problems that involve adding or subtracting fractions using the appropriate solving strategies and tools.
After this lesson, you should be able to multiply simple fractions and mixed fractions.

After this lesson, you should be able to solve both routine and non-routine problems that involve multiplying fractions and mixed numbers with or without addition or subtraction using appropriate problem-solving strategies and tools.
After this lesson, you should be able to divide simple fractions and mixed numbers.

After this lesson, you should be able to solve both routine and non-routine problems that involve dividing fractions and mixed numbers with or without any of the other operations, using appropriate problem-solving strategies and tools.
After this lesson, you should be able to add and subtract decimals and mixed decimals up to ten thousandths, with or without regrouping.

After this lesson, you should be able to solve 1 or more steps of routine and non-routine problems that involve adding and/or subtracting decimals and mixed decimals. You can use the appropriate problem-solving strategies and tools to do this.
After completing this lesson, you should be able to multiply decimals and mixed decimals with up to 2 decimal places.
After going through this lesson, you are expected to multiply mentally decimals up to 2 decimal places by 0.1, 0.01, 10, and 100.

After this lesson, you should be able to solve both routine and non-routine problems that involve multiplying decimals and mixed decimals, including money, using appropriate problem-solving strategies.

After this lesson, you should be able to solve multi-step problems that involve multiplying and adding or subtracting decimals, mixed decimals, and whole numbers, including money, using the appropriate problem-solving strategies and tools.

After completing this lesson, you should be able to divide whole numbers by decimals with up to two decimal places and also divide decimals by whole numbers and mixed decimals with up to two decimal places.
After this lesson, you should be able to divide decimals with up to four decimal places by 0.1, 0.01, and 0.001, and decimals with up to two decimal places by 10, 100, and 1,000 in your head.
After this lesson, you should be able to tell the difference between decimal numbers that end (terminating) and those that go on forever in a repeating pattern (repeating, non-terminating).

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to solve routine and non-routine problems involving the division of decimals, mixed decimals, whole numbers, and money using effective problem-solving strategies and tools.

This lesson will help you solve complex, multi-step problems involving division with decimals, whole numbers, and money. You\'ll learn to apply effective problem-solving strategies and tools, building confidence to tackle real-world problems with these operations.
Upon completing this lesson, you should be able to express one value as a fraction of another based on their ratio and do the reverse as well.
After this lesson, you should be able to explain and understand ratio and proportion.
After this lesson, you should be able to find the percentage, rate, and base in a given problem and also solve both routine and non-routine problems involving these concepts.

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to solve a variety of problems involving percentages, including discounts, original prices, discount rates, sale prices, markup prices, commissions, sales tax, and simple interest and principal. You will also learn how to calculate Percentage, Rate, and Base.
This lesson will help you understand exponents and bases in numbers written in exponential notation, as well as the importance of this topic in various mathematical operations.

After this lesson, we will learn the order of operations used to simplify expressions. The order of operations refers to the sequence in which steps must be followed to correctly simplify an expression, based on specific rules for each set of operations.

In this lesson, we will explore the set of integers and identify real-life situations where they are used. In the number system, there are two main categories: real numbers and imaginary numbers. Integers are classified as real numbers.
In the previous lesson, we explored integers and the basic concept of the number line. In this topic, we will compare and arrange integers on the number line.
In this lesson, we will also explore how to interpret and describe the basic operations of integers are addition and subtraction using materials such as algebra tiles, counters, or chips.
In this lesson, we will learn how to perform basic operations with integers.
In this lesson, you will learn how to solve both routine and non-routine problems involving the basic operations of integers, using the appropriate strategies and tools.

In this lesson, we will explore basic geometry concepts and learn how to describe the shapes we see around us. We will look at pictures of different figures and talk about how geometry appears in everyday objects. We will also learn about different solid figures and their common characteristics.

In this module, we will explore additional concepts in algebra. We\'ll develop strategies for finding the nth term of a sequence by using various methods, such as identifying patterns, making educated guesses, and working backward. Additionally, we\'ll focus on distinguishing between expressions and equations.
In this lesson, we will focus on translating real-life word expressions and equations into letters and vice versa.
This time in this lesson, we will focus and practice on how to represent quantities in real-life situations using algebraic expressions and equations.

In this lesson, you will learn the mathematical relation between speed, distance, and time. You will calculate speed based on the distance traveled and the time taken and also solve problems that involve average rate and speed.

In this lesson, you will learn how to apply the concept of finding the area of composite figures in real-life situations. By the end, you\'ll be able to clearly visualize different composite shapes and solve problems related to their areas.

In this lesson, you will explore how to visualize the surface area of various solid figures, including cubes, prisms, pyramids, cones, cylinders, and spheres. You\'ll also learn the formulas used to calculate surface area. Surface area is defined as the total sum of the areas of all the surfaces of a solid shape.

By the end of the lesson, you will be able to understand and use formulas to calculate the surface area of cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones, and spheres and apply it to real-life situations. You will also practice solving problems related to the surface area of these shapes.
In this lesson, we will focus on how to determine the relationship of volume between a rectangular prism and a pyramid; a cylinder and a cone; a cylinder and a sphere.

In this lesson, we will explore the volume of solid figures and practice solving both routine and non-routine problems related to their volumes. We will also derive formulas to calculate volume in cubic units.
In this lesson, we will learn how to read and understand electric and water meter readings. You will also practice recording, interpreting, and writing these meter readings.
In this lesson, we will explore pie graphs and learn how to create them. However, before focusing on pie graphs, it\'s important to cover some basic concepts about measuring angles.
In this lesson, we will learn how to solve both routine and non-routine problems using data presented in a pie chart.
In this lesson, you will learn how to explain the concept of probability, using examples like a 50% chance of rain or a one-in-a-million chance of winning.
This time we will focus on making listings and diagrams of outcomes and tell the number of favorable outcomes and chances using these listings and diagrams.
In this lesson, we will focus on making simple predictions of events using theoretical and experimental probability.
In this lesson, we will focus on solving both routine and non-routine problems related to experimental and theoretical probability.
Complete this lesson to master the concepts.
